stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is appropriately licensed for a proposed compounding activity and plans to compound a drug that is hazardous under the applicable standards. Which principles should the pharmacist apply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Continue to follow the sterile or non-sterile compounding requirements applicable to the preparation.
Apply the current hazardous-drug handling requirements that govern the hazardous ingredient and compounding process.
Treat hazardous-drug status as replacing all other compounding requirements.
Ignore hazardous-drug controls if the prescription is patient-specific.
Use the fact that the pharmacy has a compounding license as proof that no additional hazardous-drug operational controls apply.

explanation.core_reasoning: Hazardous-drug compounding requires concurrent analysis. The pharmacy must satisfy the compounding framework applicable to the preparation and the hazardous-drug handling standards. Neither framework displaces the other merely because the prescription is patient-specific or the pharmacy already holds a compounding license.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: the underlying sterile or non-sterile compounding requirements still apply.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: hazardous-drug handling requirements are an additional operational layer.
choice_analysis.C: Hazardous status does not replace the compounding framework.
choice_analysis.D: Patient-specific status does not erase hazardous-drug obligations.
choice_analysis.E: Licensure does not itself satisfy every operational hazardous-drug standard.

explanation.mpje_trap: The legal frameworks stack; they do not substitute for each other.

reasoning_steps: Classify both the type of compounding and the hazardous-drug status
Apply the compounding framework and hazardous-drug framework concurrently
Reject choices that treat one compliance framework as cancelling the other
